plate_findings.evidence: ONB at the superior part of both nasal cavities

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Contrast-enhanced coronal CT panel from a 70-year-old woman with anosmia, captioned as showing olfactory neuroblastoma at the typical superior nasal cavity location with bilateral ethmoid and intracranial extension. B: Axial contrast-enhanced CT panel from the same case, captioned as showing olfactory neuroblastoma at the typical superior nasal cavity location with bilateral ethmoid and intracranial extension. C: Coronal brain CT obtained 4 years earlier, captioned as showing soft tissue in the slightly expanded left olfactory recess most likely representing a small unrecognized ONB. D: Axial brain CT obtained 4 years earlier, captioned as showing soft tissue in the slightly expanded left olfactory recess most likely representing a small unrecognized ONB.

panels.figure_caption: Typical location of olfactory neuroblastoma (ONB), shown in a 70-year-old woman presenting with anosmia. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) images showed ONB at the superior part of both nasal cavities with bilateral ethmoid sinuses and intracranial extension (A-B). Brain CT performed 4 years prior due to headache (C-D) showed soft tissue in the slightly expanded left olfactory recess, most likely representing a small ONB that went unrecognized at that time.
in_text_mentions: Fifty patients (86.2%) had the epicenter of the mass in the superior part of the nasal cavity. One patient in this group had a CT scan performed 4 years prior due to headache (Figure 1).

plate_findings.evidence: Conventional ONB (top left)

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 5 panels (A, B, C, D, E). A: H&E histology panel captioned as clear cell change in olfactory neuroblastoma, a recognized morphologic variant. B: H&E histology panel captioned as oncocytic change in olfactory neuroblastoma. C: H&E histology panel captioned as spindle cell change, more common in high-grade olfactory neuroblastoma. D: H&E panel shows conventional olfactory neuroblastoma transitioning to spindled stroma with inset ganglion cells, indicating ganglioneuronal differentiation. E: Immunohistochemical panel showing S100 positivity in spindled stroma and NeuN-positive ganglion cells in olfactory neuroblastoma with ganglioneuronal differentiation.
panels.attribution_text: Gargano et al. Refinement of Hyams Grading Criteria for Olfactory Neuroblastoma in an Endoscopic Sinus Surgery Predominant Cohort with Extended Follow-up: Worth the Effort?. Head and neck pathology 2025. doi:10.1007/s12105-025-01804-z. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 3.
panels.figure_caption: Other morphologies. A) Clear cell (40x), and B) oncocytic (40x) change were fairly common. C) Spindle cell change was somewhat more common in high grade tumors (20x). D,E: Ganglioneuronal differentiation. D) Conventional ONB (top left) transitioning to a spindled stroma (4x). Inset: Scattered embedded ganglion cells (40x). E) The spindled stroma is S100 positive. Inset: A subset of ganglion cells was Neuronal nuclear protein positive (40x)
in_text_mentions: Other key features are illustrated in Fig. 3. Clear cell/oncocytic change (53%, 31/59) and spindling (22%, 13/59) were not uncommon in our cohort, but did not vary significantly between grade groups though spindling was somewhat more frequent in high grade tumors. Similarly, ganglioneuromatous stroma though rare, did not vary between grade groups.

A: H&E panel from an olfactory neuroblastoma cohort showing gland entrapment with mucous cell predominance, a specific epithelial interaction described in the disease context. Head and neck pathology 2025. doi:10.1007/s12105-025-01804-z. CC BY (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/). Figure 4.
panels.figure_caption: Spectrum of epithelial interactions. A) Gland entrapment with glands showing prominent mucous cell predominance (10x). B) Gland entrapment with proliferative change with complex back-to-back seromucinous glands (10x). Inset (40x): The nuclei of the seromucinous glands are considerably smaller than those of the tumor (left of inset). C) Surface or intraepithelial involvement with accumulation of lesional cells basally (10x). Inset (20x): Intraepithelial component highlighted by an SSTR2 immunostain. D-F: Olfactory neuroblastoma with divergent epithelial differentiation (olfactory carcinoma). D) Anastomosing reticular patterned eosinophilic epithelium admixed with the ONB component (10x, inset: 40x). E) The tumor shows synaptophysin staining of the ONB component (10x) along with S100 staining of sustentacular cells (inset: 10x). F) Cytokeratin AE1/3 highlights an inverse pattern, restricted to the epithelial component
in_text_mentions: Only one case (2%) in the low-grade group showed a surface intraepithelial component. Epithelial interactions with seromucinous glands on the other hand were overall somewhat more frequent in the high-grade group, but not significantly so. While divergent epithelial differentiation was exclusive to the high-grade group, only three cases were noted (5%). The spectrum of epithelial interaction is shown in Fig. 4.

panels.figure_caption: Microscopic pathology of the lesion. A–C Small round blue cell morphology. Immunohistochemistry confirmed metastatic ONB (CgA+, Syn+, CD56+), explaining the misdiagnosis based on imaging alone
in_text_mentions: The patient underwent open liver resection. Postoperative gross pathology (Fig. 4) revealed a well-circumscribed mass with a gray-white to gray-yellow cut surface. Microscopic examination (Fig. 5) showed a malignant small blue cell tumor. Immunohistochemistry demonstrated positivity for chromogranin A (CgA), synaptophysin (Syn), and CD56, with a Ki-67 labeling index of approximately 30%, consistent with hepatic metastatic ONB, in light of the patient’s clinical history.

panels.figure_caption: T1 weighted axial MRI
in_text_mentions: MRI with contrast showed a large enhancing mass, with possible intrinsic bone formation, measuring 7.6 x 2.2 x 6.3 cm (Figures 1-3). The mass extended into the left nasal cavity, inferiorly into the nasopharynx, and superiorly into the anterior cranial fossa. It was noted that there was a destruction of the ethmoid sinus along with mass effects on the left medial rectus muscle and the left optic nerve without an abnormal signal in the optic nerves. The mass displaced the optic chiasm superiorly.

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 4 panels (A, B, C, D). A: Panel A shows tumor cells with diffuse and strong cytoplasmic positivity for NSE by immunohistochemistry in a patient with olfactory neuroblastoma. NSE positivity is a supportive neuroendocrine marker but is not represented in the allowed finding vocabulary. B: Panel B demonstrates diffuse and strong cytoplasmic chromogranin A positivity in olfactory neuroblastoma tumor cells, matching the allowed chromogranin positivity finding for this disease. C: Panel C shows S100 immunohistochemistry highlighting sustentacular cells at the periphery of tumor lobules, a characteristic supporting feature of olfactory neuroblastoma. This specific S100 pattern is not in the allowed finding vocabulary. D: Panel D shows focal cytokeratin AE1/AE3 positivity in olfactory neuroblastoma tumor cells. Cytokeratin immunoreactivity is variable in olfactory neuroblastoma and is not represented in the allowed finding vocabulary.

Kadish C/Hyams II Esthesioneuroblastoma With Atypical Immunophenotype Mimicking NK/T-Cell Lymphoma: Endoscope-Assisted Transcranial Resection and Adjuvant Intensity-Modulated Radiotherapy.. panels.figure_caption: Immunohistochemistry (IHC) panel. (A) CD3: negative in neoplastic cells (appropriate internal/external controls). (B) CD20: negative in neoplastic cells (controls adequate). (C) CD56: diffuse membranous/cytoplasmic positivity in tumor cells. (D) Ki-67: proliferation index ~40% in hot spots. (E) Chromogranin A: negative. (F) Granzyme B: negative. (G) TIA-1: negative. (H) S100 protein: sustentacular pattern highlights peripheral sustentacular cells encasing tumor nests. (I) Synaptophysin: negative. Interpretation: The combination of CD56 positivity with a sustentacular S100 pattern and absence of B-/T-cell and cytotoxic markers (CD3, CD20, TIA-1, granzyme B), together with the lack of classic neuroendocrine markers (chromogranin/synaptophysin) and the histomorphology, supports Hyams Grade II esthesioneuroblastoma and argues against extranodal NK/T-cell lymphoma.
in_text_mentions: The initial biopsy reported a poorly differentiated malignant neoplasm with a differential diagnosis of nasal NK/T-cell lymphoma versus ENB. Slide review with a targeted IHC panel showed CD56 positivity with a sustentacular S100 pattern, Ki-67 30%-40%, and negativity for CD3, CD20, chromogranin, granzyme B, TIA-1, and synaptophysin (Figure 5 and Figure 6).

panels.rationale: Whole-figure plate of 2 panels (a, b). a: Coronal 18F-FDG PET/CT of the head/face at diagnosis in a patient with ectopic ACTH-secreting olfactory neuroblastoma; the solid white arrow marks the intensely hypermetabolic ethmoidal tumor extending into the nasal cavities, matching the target disease's primary sinonasal manifestation. b: Coronal whole-body 18F-FDG PET of the same olfactory neuroblastoma patient at diagnosis; dotted arrows mark a left apical pulmonary nodule and bilateral adrenal hyperplasia (ectopic ACTH hyperstimulation). The scan is the staging/diagnostic PET of the FDG-avid sinonasal neuroblastoma, though the highlighted secondary findings (pulmonary nodule, adrenal hyperplasia) are not themselves direct tumor manifestations, lowering confidence.
